Markers · Join it · Lesson 1 · B2B customer service

Although the truck is late, but we ship today.
Although the truck is late, we ship today.

Four small words that join two ideas: because, so, although and while. Each idea has its own subject and verb, and some of these words sound like speech while others sound like writing.

Dotted is a work word you can learn. Passe o mouse ou toque para ver a tradução. Não é o foco da aula: o foco são os markers.

Primeiro, o ouvido: qual frase soa natural e como você diria em cinco segundos. Depois, a ideia por trás dos quatro markers e uma camada sobre como as pessoas realmente os usam na fala e na escrita, com a fonte de cada afirmação. Em seguida, sete exercícios de prática, três de ouvir e um role-play. O botão Join it, no canto, abre a consulta a qualquer momento.

2Idea

Join two ideas

Um marker liga duas ideias completas, cada uma com o seu sujeito e o seu verbo

A marker joins two full ideas. Each idea has its own subject and its own verb.

Nada de nome solto: depois do marker vem uma frase inteira. O marker diz qual é a relação entre as duas: razão, resultado, contraste.

idea 1 marker idea 2

  1. becauseWhy?

    We can’t deliver today because our driver is sick.

    Because dá a razão. A razão vem depois dele.

    a razão
  2. soWhat happens next?

    Our driver is sick, so we can’t deliver today.

    So mostra o resultado. Para ligar duas ideias, ele fica no meio, depois de uma vírgula.

    o resultado
  3. althoughEven so?

    Although our driver is sick, we can deliver today.

    Although liga duas coisas que não combinam, e mesmo assim aconteceu. Even though é o although com mais ênfase.

    mesmo assim
  4. whileSide by side?

    Our warehouse in Brazil is full while the one in Chile is empty.

    While põe dois lados lado a lado: ao mesmo tempo, ou um em contraste com o outro.

    dois lados
e a ordem?

Three markers can move. So stays in the middle.

Because, although e while podem abrir a frase. Aí a primeira ideia termina com vírgula. O so, quando liga duas ideias, fica sempre no meio. (Um “So,” no começo de uma fala é outra coisa: a seção Speaking and writing explica.)

because

We can’t deliver today because our driver is sick.

Because our driver is sick, we can’t deliver today.

although

Although our driver is sick, we can deliver today.

We can deliver today although our driver is sick.

while

While our warehouse in Brazil is full, the one in Chile is empty.

Our warehouse in Brazil is full while the one in Chile is empty.

so

Our driver is sick, so we can’t deliver today. só assim

A vírgula laranja entra quando o marker abre a frase. Quando ele fica no meio, não há vírgula (exceto antes de so).

só um!

One marker for each link. Never two.

O português deixa passar “porque... então”. O inglês escolhe um só. Quem corrige é a caneta do professor.

Although the invoice is small, buttira! we must pay it.

Because the carrier is on strike, sotira! we will wait.

+ nome ou + frase?

After because and while, a full idea. After because of and during, only a noun.

Se tem sujeito e verbo, use because ou while. Se é só um nome (the road, the loading), use because of ou during.

because + idea

The truck stopped because the road was closed.

porque + frase

because of + noun

The truck stopped because of the closed road.

por causa de + nome

while + idea

I called the customer while the truck was loading.

enquanto + frase

during + noun

I called the customer during the loading.

durante + nome

3Register

Speaking and writing

Como as pessoas realmente usam esses markers: o que soa como fala e o que soa como escrita

The same marker can feel different on the phone and in a report.

Cada linha abaixo diz de onde vem a informação. Assim você sabe o que é fato de uma fonte, o que foi contado em textos reais e o que é leitura nossa.

Source saysUm material de referência diz isso com todas as letras. O link está na linha.
CountedContamos em textos reais. Os números mostram uma direção, não uma medida exata.
Our readingUma conclusão nossa a partir do que está acima. Não é um fato de fonte.
becausespeech and writing
In speech3.7In writing0.9Times per 1,000 words · phone talk × business news
Source saysOne of the five everyday linkers for IELTS Speaking (and, but, because, also, like), and you can repeat it. In formal exam writing, avoid opening a sentence with “Because” or “Because of”: use “Owing to” or “Due to”. (IELTS Liz · Speaking, IELTS Liz · Writing) This is exam advice, not a rule of English.
CountedAbout four times more frequent in phone talk than in business news.
Our readingOn the phone, “because” is the natural answer to “why?”. In a report, the opening version with a noun is “owing to” or “due to”.
sospeech first
In speech32%In writing6%Share of all “so” that open a sentence · phone talk × business news
Counted153 of the 474 “so” in phone talk open a sentence; in business news, 26 of 409. Real line: “So I got an opportunity to transfer back, and I took it.”
Source saysFor formal writing, Liz lists as a result, consequently, therefore and thus as result linkers. Her writing list also has “so”, with no warning. (IELTS Liz · Writing)
Our readingIn conversation, an opening “So,” does not join two ideas inside one sentence: it moves the story forward, what happened next. To join two ideas in a report, “therefore” and “as a result” do that job.
althoughspeech and writing
In speech0.27In writing0.24Times per 1,000 words · phone talk × business news
Source saysAfter “although”, a subject and a verb. (British Council) “Although” tends to be used in a more formal context than “though”. (Grammarly)
CountedThe same in both: it works in speech and in writing.
Our readingAlthough and but do the same job, so only one goes in. This is the standard classroom rule; I did not find an open source to cite for it.
whilewriting a bit more
In speech0.30In writing0.75Times per 1,000 words · phone talk × business news
Source says“While” is on Liz’s contrast list for Speaking, with but, although and on the other hand. (IELTS Liz · Speaking)
CountedTwo and a half times more frequent in business news. The count mixes the “at the same time” and the “contrast” meanings. In phone talk, “but” appears 540 times and “while” 19.
Our readingFor a simple contrast in speech, but is the easy choice. Use while when you put two facts side by side.
thoughbonus · speech
In speech50%In writing0%Share of all “though” that end the sentence · phone talk × business news
Source says“Though can also go at the end of the second phrase. This way of expressing contrasting ideas is most common in spoken English.” (British Council) “Though” is the more casual option. (Grammarly)
Counted10 of the 20 “though” in phone talk end the sentence; none of the 53 in business news. Real line: “I do worry about medical, though.”
Our readingUse it in conversation to soften a contrast: “It’s expensive. We need it, though.” In a report, use however or although.

Where the numbers come from. Phone conversations in US English (about 64,000 words) and Reuters business news from 1987. They are not work emails, and the phone sample is small, so use the numbers as a direction. The Cambridge and Collins dictionaries were not available to us, so they are not cited here.

At work. Phone with a customer: because, so, though. Email or report: because, although, therefore, owing to. (Our reading, from everything above.)

4Practice

Reason, result or contrast?

Razão, resultado ou contraste? Escolha o marker que fecha a ligação

Tap the marker that fits the blank.

Leia as duas ideias e pergunte: uma explica a outra (because), uma é consequência da outra (so) ou uma contraria a outra (although)?

Example · exemplo resolvido

The customer is upset because the delivery was two days late.

A razão vem depois: a entrega atrasou, por isso ele está chateado.

  9. 9

4

Because or because of?

Because ou because of? Depende do que vem depois

Tap the one that fits: a full idea or only a noun?

Depois do espaço, tem sujeito e verbo ou só um nome? Sujeito e verbo pedem because. Só um nome pede because of.

Example · exemplo resolvido

We stopped the line because of a power problem.

“A power problem” é um nome, sem verbo. Nome pede “because of”.

5

While or during?

While ou during? A mesma pergunta: uma frase inteira ou um nome?

Tap the one that fits.

While também liga dois lados em contraste. Se o que vem depois tem sujeito e verbo, é while.

Example · exemplo resolvido

Please don’t call the driver during the trip.

“The trip” é um nome. Nome pede “during”.

Your turn · agora é você
  1. 1

    I check the stock my colleague loads the truck.

    “My colleague loads the truck” é uma frase inteira: “while”.

  2. 2

    The line stopped the night shift.

    “The night shift” é um nome (um período): “during”.

  3. 3

    Please keep your phone off the meeting.

    “The meeting” é um nome: “during”.

  4. 4

    Plant A is full plant B is almost empty.

    Duas frases em contraste, lado a lado: “while”.

  5. 5

    Sales are up in Brazil they are down in Chile.

    Duas frases em contraste: “while”.

  6. 6

    Don’t call the driver he is driving.

    “He is driving” tem sujeito e verbo: “while”.

  7. 7

    The customer called three times the week.

    “The week” é um período: “during”.

8

Speaking or writing?

Fala ou escrita? Onde essa frase soa mais natural

Where does this sentence sound more natural?

Use a seção Speaking and writing. É uma tendência, não uma lei: pense no que soa mais natural.

Example · exemplo resolvido

So, did you check the stock?

“So,” abrindo a frase é conversa. No relatório, a ligação vem de outro jeito.

Your turn · agora é você
  1. 1

    ’Cause the truck broke down, so we’re late.

    “’Cause” é a forma falada de because.

  2. 2

    Consequently, two lines were stopped.

    “Consequently” é de texto formal. Na conversa, ficaria “so”.

  3. 3

    I like the price. It’s a bit high, though.

    “Though” no fim da frase é de fala.

  4. 4

    So I called the carrier, and he said Friday.

    Contando o que aconteceu, a conversa abre com “So”.

  5. 5

    So, did you get the invoice?

    “So” abrindo a frase é típico de conversa.

  6. 6

    Owing to the strike, delivery will be delayed.

    “Owing to” é de texto formal (a IELTS Liz recomenda para a escrita).

  7. 7

    The batch passed all tests. Therefore, we recommend approval.

    “Therefore” é formal: aparece muito mais na escrita e em discursos formais do que na conversa.

Though at the end

Though no fim: o contraste em tom de conversa

Say it like a conversation: two short sentences, and “though” at the end of the second.

Troque o “but” por um ponto. O “though” vai para o fim da segunda frase, depois de uma vírgula.

Example · exemplo resolvido

The deadline is short, but we can do it.

The deadline is short. We can do it, though.

O contraste vai para o fim da segunda frase, em tom de conversa.

    O preço é alto. Mas eu gosto.

  3. 3

    It is expensive, but we need it.

    É caro. Mas nós precisamos.

  4. 4

    O caminhão está atrasado. Mas a qualidade está boa.

11True or false?

Ouça a frase e diga se a afirmação é verdadeira. Atenção: although junta duas coisas que aconteceram.

Example · exemplo resolvido

You hear“Although the shipment was small, it cost a lot.”

The shipment was big.

“Although” junta duas coisas verdadeiras: era pequena e custou muito.

Markers · Lesson 1
Join it
becausewhy?

We can’t deliver because our driver is sick.

Opens the sentence? Comma after idea 1. Before a noun: because of.

sowhat next?

Our driver is sick, so we can’t deliver.

Always in the middle, comma before. Often opens a sentence in speech.

althougheven so?

Although our driver is sick, we can deliver.

No “but” in the same sentence. In speech, “though” at the end does a similar job.

whileside by side

Warehouse A is full while B is empty.

Before a noun: during.

one markerper link

Because…, so … · Although…, but …

Speaking: because, so, though. Writing: although, therefore, owing to.
